summary: Round 2 (commit 1c0735d) resolves all three round-1 findings without regressions. (1) Focus ring: the new `.tm-follow-ups .tm-follow-ups__remove:focus-visible` rule (0,3,0) outranks the (0,2,0) remove rule. It has the same specificity as the combined `...__remove:hover` rule that also sets `box-shadow: none`, but it is declared later, so the ring stays visible while the button is both hovered and focused. The only Obsidian rules for this state in /opt/Obsidian/resources/obsidian.asar are `button:focus-visible` (0,1,1) and `button.mod-cta:focus-visible` (0,2,1, which does not match), so nothing outranks it. The value matches Obsidian's native ring, and the button's color and background are unchanged. (2) Accessible name: the pending-row input now has aria-label={$t('followUps.placeholder')}, and the key exists in both en.ts and ru.ts. Created rows have no input, so nothing is missing there. (3) Prototype: `inputs` is now Object.create(null) (confirmed in the built main.js: `s=Object.create(null)` with the binding `s[v.id]=k`). An id of '__proto__' therefore becomes an own key instead of calling the inherited setter. The `Record<string, HTMLInputElement | null>` annotation is sound because Object.create returns `any`. Optional chaining in `inputs[id]?.focus()`, `delete inputs[id]`, and bind:this assignment and null teardown all work the same on a prototype-less object. Side note, not caused by this fix and harmless: Svelte's bind:this teardown sets `inputs[id] = null` after remove() runs `delete inputs[id]`, so a null entry stays behind for each removed row for the lifetime of the component. I was asked not to run tests, so I did not. The executor reports npm run build and 39/39 e2e passing.
